subject.title: Discord routing: mention > reply-target > default owner (suppress default owner when targeted)

question: Should Discord multi-bot inbound routing adopt strict active-target precedence that suppresses the per-channel default owner whenever an explicit bot mention or native reply target identifies another configured bot?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but the fix changes existing default-owner and binding behavior for multi-bot Discord deployments, so maintainer product intent is needed before an automated repair should proceed.

options.title: Accept strict active-target precedence
options.body: Implement Discord-owned mention and reply-target selection before default routing, preserve untagged default-owner behavior, and require focused tests plus live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep current default-owner contract
options.body: Leave default/binding routing as the primary contract and close or supersede this issue with docs explaining that explicit bindings or existing policies are required.

options.title: Narrow to reply policy only
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80235 as the only intended change and leave cross-bot mention/default-owner suppression for a separate design.

recommendation.title: Accept strict active-target precedence
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned mention and reply-target selection before default routing, preserve untagged default-owner behavior, and require focused tests plus live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history and prior review comments point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for deciding the Discord mention/routing contract.
